findings.reason: a node implementing §7 will run this test red and must decide whether to rewrite it (superseding the pin, as §2 did) or add a zero-section guard that keeps such a plan blocked; without the plan stating which, the two readings send it to opposite mechanisms for the same plan shape.
findings.text: §7 delivers "A gate whose `gated_sections` is non-empty holds those sections only", which for a plan whose only gate names sections makes the plan read ready, yet `tests/test_roadmap.py:1394` (`test_gate_verdict_blocks_and_releases_downstream_sections_without_status_edit`) pins the opposite for exactly that shape — a gate `gated_sections: ["deployment","release"]`, `verdict: "failed"` asserted to give `discovered[0]["effective_status"] == "blocked"`, `roadmap["blocked"][0]["effective_status"] == "blocked"` and `roadmap["ready_now"] == []` (test_roadmap.py:1418-1423), and under §7 that gate is section-holding so the plan is neither blocked nor absent from `ready_now`; §2 names the test it supersedes ("which pins the behaviour this section supersedes"), but §7 names none, and the case that decides the outcome — a plan with no implementable section declarations, where the third clause "a plan whose every implementable section is gated is held by those gates" is vacuously true and so contradicts the primary rule — is left undefined by either sentence
